Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:149669
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 32484 of 2024

Applicant :- Mukesh Kumar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Kumar Ashutosh Srivastava,Nagendra Bahadur Singh
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Nagendra Bahadur Singh, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Imran Khan,
learned AGA, for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been moved on behalf of the applicant with the prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No.184 of 2020, under Sections 406,420,467,468,471,120B,323, 504 and 506 IPC, Police Station Kotwali Farrukhabad, District Farrukhabad during pendency of the trial.

entities.text: Police Station Kotwali Farrukhabad, District Farrukhabad
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that FIR of the present case was lodged against three accused persons(non applicant) and as per allegation, the Company of nominated accused duped the common public and misappropriated more than Rs. Seven Crores but during investigation applicant has been made accused in the present matter on the ground that he was also one of the Director in the Company.

4. He further submits that applicant was nominated as Director in Prestige Developers India Private Limited in the year 2009 by Chief Managing Director and he resigned from the Company in the year Mukesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103751228/
1 2011 and at the time of alleged misappropriation he was not in the Company.

entities.text: Mukesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He next submits that in this regard a specific averment has been made in paragraph-12 of the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application.
5. He further submits that if after resignation of the applicant from the company, the company and its Director duped the common public then applicant cannot be held liable.
6. He further submits that apart from the present case applicant is having criminal history of two other cases but his criminal history has been explained in the instant bail application.

7. He further submits that all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate First Class and in the present matter applicant is in jail since 18.5.2023, i.e., for the last more than a year.
8.
Per contra, learned AGA, however, opposed the prayerfor bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant.
9. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

10. However, as per allegation applicant was one of the Director in Prestige Developers India Private Limited and his Company duped the common public and misappropriated more than Rs. Seven Crore but it reflects that applicant was not named in the FIR and during investigation he was made accused on the ground that he was also one of the Director of the Company but in paragraph-12 of the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application applicant specifically averred that he had resigned from the Company in the year 2011 and this fact has not been controverted by learned AGA.

11. Further, there is also no evidence on record which can show that applicant was either In charge for day-today business of the Company or he was the person, who either received the money from the investors or on his instructions money was deposited.

12. Further, however, it appears that apart from the present case applicant is having criminal history of two other cases but his criminal antecedent has been explained in the instant bail application.
13.
Further, all the alleged offences are triable by Magistrate First Class and applicant is in jail in the present matter since 18.5.2023, i.e., for the last more than a year.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

16. Let the applicant-Mukesh Kumar be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned Mukesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103751228/
2 with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.

sentences.text: 17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 13.9.2024 SKM  Mukesh Kumar vs State Of U.P. on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103751228/
